verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents official client libraries in multiple languages, with C++ and Python APIs verified at install. Code generators produce typed message interfaces across those libraries, and the Python library uses native types. However, the docs state that intra-process communication, composition, managed lifecycles and content filtering are "Currently only in C++", so the Python library does not cover the full surface. Missing for 10: any evidence of TypeScript or Go SDKs, full feature parity across languages (several features are C++-only), and independent corroboration of SDK quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build against official, typed SDKs in multiple languages (Python, TypeScript, Go, C++) that cover the platform's full surface

citations.quote: Client libraries come in a variety of programming languages so that users may write ROS 2 code in the language that is best-suited for their application.
This verifies both the C++ and Python APIs are working properly.
Nodes written using different client libraries are able to share messages with each other because all client libraries implement code generators
The interface provides an idiomatic Python experience that uses native Python types and patterns like lists and context objects.
Support for nodes with managed lifecycles - Currently only in C++.
Composition of node components at compile, link, load, or run time - Currently only in C++.
